source: genuine OCI Playwright screen recording and original Relate impact receipt

music.source: original procedural composition; no external samples

scenes.name: intro
scenes.voice: Most data problems don't begin with a dramatic failure. They begin with one small change.

scenes.name: change
scenes.voice: Here, a lab field called moisture percent changes from a number out of a hundred to a fraction. The column name stays. Its meaning doesn't.

scenes.name: path
scenes.voice: Data Impact Graph opens a real, embedded Relate database, and follows its Cypher paths. First the assay is normalized. Then dry mass is calculated.

scenes.name: fork
scenes.voice: And now, the interesting part. That same dry-mass calculation feeds two teams that might never speak to each other.

scenes.name: finance
scenes.voice: Finance uses payable dry kilograms to forecast supplier payouts. A quiet unit change can reach the money.

scenes.name: climate
scenes.voice: Climate uses dry tonnes to calculate carbon intensity. The dependency chain reaches the Scope Three assurance dashboard.

scenes.name: negative
scenes.voice: Change the field identifier instead, and neither payout nor carbon is affected. Good lineage analysis needs to know when not to raise the alarm.

scenes.name: receipt
scenes.voice: Before merging, export the impact receipt. It gives a reviewer the affected outputs, actual dependency paths, and why every connection matters.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.voice: One embedded graph. Forty-nine assets. Sixty relationships. Know what breaks before you change it. Data Impact Graph.
